scratchBlock.LESSON: A declaration list no control reads stays stale indefinitely. `design-completion-gate.mjs` reads `_design/INDEX.md` and `_design/surface_coverage.json` and never reads `_design/all-canvas/build.mjs`, so the canvas's surface list is a fourth declaration surface with no watcher — the omission sat there unnoticed and fixing it cannot move the gate. Before declaring a declaration fixed, ask which control reads it; if the answer is none, the fix is invisible and needs its own instrument.

A pre-flight on board DIMENSIONS is not a pre-flight on board NAMES. I verified all eleven new boards parsed on the canvas's root-dimension pattern and then transcribed one folder's entry board as `Main.dc.html`, which that folder does not have. Take file names and captions from the folder's own `canvas.json` rather than typing them; it costs one command and removes a whole class of error.

A translation at build time hides the source defect from every consumer that does not run the build. The right evidence shape for 'fixed at source' is a MATCH COUNT of the translation's own patterns before and after (13 -> 0), not a sentence saying the strings are gone.
scratchBlock.DEAD-END: Running `design-instrument-exits.mjs --violate` inside the lane worktree. It refuses on a dirty `_design` tree by design, and even on a clean tree it plants defects into every other folder, including a sibling lane's — which the dispatch forbids. A `git clone` of the worktree with the lane's files committed gives a clean tree whose run cannot reach another lane's folders.

`fc /b` on two 350 KB single-line HTML files to characterise a difference. It prints the whole file and every offset looks different after the first length change. Compare lengths, then pin the difference as one contiguous deletion by common prefix/suffix and account for the bytes.
